originalPreBoundary:
At my first dinner with my partner’s family, his mother introduced me to a neighbor as “his friend.”

We had been together for two years. We were both adults.

My partner heard the introduction and kept setting the table.

His mother was paying our rent while I looked for work.

The neighbor smiled at me and waited.

I was standing by the table, close enough to speak to the neighbor and for my partner and his mother to hear. I could say I was his partner, or let this introduction pass.

I wanted to be recognized as his partner. I was also afraid of putting the rent help at risk; I did not know whether she would stop helping or why she had used “friend.”

evidenceFacts.claim: At my first family dinner, his mother introduced me to a neighbor as “his friend.”
We had been together for two years and were adults.
My partner heard the introduction and kept setting the table.
His mother paid our rent while I looked for work.
The neighbor smiled at me and waited.
I stood by the table, could speak within their hearing, and could correct the introduction or let it pass.
I wanted recognition and feared risking rent help; withdrawal and the mother’s reason were unknown.

unknowns: What my partner was thinking then.
Whether correcting would change rent assistance.
Whether the family already recognized the relationship elsewhere.

neutral: Anonymous adult silhouettes for all four people. No gender presentation inferred for the narrator.
Table setting represented by a single place-setting motion then a held task pose; plates are neutral set dressing, not persistent interactable objects.
Ordinary domestic light, warm paper and muted fabric; mother and hero receive equal exposure.
All actors are within ordinary hearing range; no invented doorway or inaccessible corner.
forbidden: Hostile mother, shamed partner posture, marriage or sexuality labels, explicit financial ultimatum, ticking dinner cue, accepting nod on silence.

revealSource.text:
I said, “I’m his partner.”

I wanted him to hear me say it. I didn’t want another evening spent pretending.

His mother changed the subject. On the way home he told me he had been afraid of losing her help.
